questions.q: Why does assigning an Azure Policy initiative at a management group scope matter more than assigning the same rules one subscription at a time?
options: The assignment inherits down to every subscription nested under that management group, including subscriptions that don't exist yet
Management group assignments are the only way to use the Audit effect
It removes the need for a landing zone entirely
It lets Azure skip the subscription-vending process from Chapter 2
questions.explain: A management-group-scoped assignment inherits to every subscription nested beneath it, so a new subscription vended next quarter is automatically covered without anyone reattaching policy.

questions.q: What is a policy initiative (policy set) in Azure Policy?
options: A single resource that stores the compliance history of one subscription
A bundle of related individual policy definitions assigned and managed together as one unit
A manual checklist reviewed once a quarter by a committee
The portal screen used to create a management group
questions.explain: Rather than assigning dozens of individual policies separately, related policies (tagging, allowed regions, encryption) are grouped into an initiative and assigned as one unit.

questions.q: What does an AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) actually do?
options: It sets a hard ceiling on allowed API actions for every identity in every account under an OU, enforced at the IAM level even against the root user
It continuously scans existing resources and reports whether they comply with a rule
It only applies inside a single AWS account, never across an OU
It automatically remediates non-compliant resources by default
questions.explain: An SCP is a preventive control attached to an OU that caps what any identity — including the account root user — is permitted to do at the API level, independent of in-account IAM policy.

questions.q: How does an AWS Config rule differ from a Service Control Policy?
options: A Config rule is also a preventive control that blocks API calls before they happen
A Config rule is a detective control that evaluates existing resources against a rule and reports compliance after the fact, rather than preventing the action
Config rules can only be used inside a single account and never across an organization
Config rules replace the need for any SCP
questions.explain: Config rules evaluate resource state after creation and report compliance (optionally triggering remediation) — the detective counterpart to an SCP's preventive blocking.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that policy definitions and SCPs should go through the same Terraform pipeline built in course 8, rather than being configured by hand in the portal?
options: Portal-based policy changes are not technically possible in Azure or AWS
Terraform is required by AWS and Azure to apply any governance rule
It produces a reviewed pull-request diff showing exactly what governance rule changed, who approved it, and when — evidence a review board or auditor can ask for directly
It eliminates the need for management groups or Organizational Units
questions.explain: Treating policy as code means every change to governance rules goes through the same plan/apply review as any other infrastructure change, producing an auditable record of who changed what and when.
